name: rustc_codegen_cranelift (Cranelift codegen backend)
baseline: cargo build (dev profile) with the default LLVM backend
verdict_reason: Cranelift does compile debug builds faster than LLVM, but the measured gains are modest: 5-12% on Zed incremental builds and 10-15% per crate on average in early 2026, and 20% wall-clock on a 2024 third-party full build. It is still nightly-only and produces slower code, so it fits dev builds only.
tier_reason: LWN's 2024 measurement is independent of the backend's author; the 2026 numbers come from the author in a rust-lang project goal, with only the core count stated.
claimed_speedup: Zed incremental build: 5% faster with debuginfo off, 12% faster with line-tables-only (February 2026, 16-core machine); single-crate builds in the rustc benchmark suite: negligible to ~30%, average 10-15%. LWN: full debug build of Cranelift 29.6 s vs 37.5 s with LLVM (20% less wall-clock), 125 vs 211 CPU-seconds (40% less)
workload: Start-to-finish incremental compilation of Zed; single-crate compiles in the rustc benchmark suite; a full debug build of the Cranelift crate with its dependencies
toolchain: nightly rustc with the rustc-codegen-cranelift-preview component; -Cdebuginfo=none and -Cdebuginfo=line-tables-only
platforms: Nightly builds on Linux, macOS and x86_64 Windows
one_liner: Nightly-only codegen backend that compiles debug builds 5-20% faster than LLVM by generating less optimized code.
how_it_is_fast: Cranelift is a code generator built to compile quickly rather than to produce the fastest code; a 2020 paper cited by LWN found it an order of magnitude faster than LLVM with code about twice as slow on some benchmarks. rustc hands it the same program it would hand LLVM, so less time goes into code generation. Parsing, type checking, linking and debuginfo are unchanged, which limits the end-to-end gain.
use_it_when: Dev builds on nightly where code generation is a large share of rebuild time
Projects that avoid the features its README lists as not yet supported
skip_it_when: Release builds: the generated code is slower
Code using std::arch SIMD intrinsics or relying on unwinding on Windows or macOS
caveats: The 2026 numbers are the backend author's, on one 16-core machine
LWN measured one crate on an unspecified machine
The front end, linker and debuginfo are unchanged, which caps the end-to-end gain
tradeoffs: Partial SIMD support; panic=abort by default

evidence.quote: In local benchmarks on a 16-core machine, as of February 2026, measuring start-to-finish incremental compilation time of Zed:
the performance benefit of the cranelift backend varies between negligible and ~30% with the average speedup around 10-15% for a single crate compilation in
A full debug build of Cranelift itself using the Cranelift backend took 29.6 seconds on my computer, compared to 37.5 with LLVM (a reduction in wall-clock time of 20%).
Compiling with Cranelift took 125 CPU-seconds, whereas LLVM took 211 CPU-seconds, a difference of 40%.
The Cranelift codegen backend is distributed in nightly builds on Linux, macOS and x86_64 Windows.
